commit.message: Add Coston2 Phase 5 evidence and relayer CLI

Add ShellCheck and TruffleHog to the static-analysis review

Completes the audit's original five-tool list (Slither/Semgrep already
covered). Installed both as prebuilt binaries from their real GitHub
release assets (resolved via the GitHub API -- ShellCheck's first guessed
asset filename was wrong and 404'd, re-derived from the actual release
listing rather than retried blindly), since apt/sudo weren't available.

ShellCheck: zero findings in either script this project authored
(scripts/generate-workproof-bindings.sh, generate-workproof-tools-bindings.sh)
or beyond-baseline in the heavily-modified pre-build.sh. One genuine defect
found in scaffold-owned testing/ infrastructure (two hook scripts with a
malformed `#\!/bin/bash` shebang instead of a real one) -- documented, not
fixed, since testing/ isn't something WorkProof invokes.

TruffleHog: one "verified" hit that's a clear false positive -- its Lob
detector matched a Python test method name
(test_version_is_plain_string_not_bytes32) as looking like a Lob API key.
Confirmed by reading the actual source line rather than trusting the
verified label. Zero real secrets found.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Bump Go toolchain 1.25.1 -> 1.25.12 and grpc, clearing all reachable govulncheck findings

The dependency-bump commit earlier today found 21 reachable vulnerabilities
in go/ (and go/'s own findings mirrored in tools/) that weren't fixable via
go.mod at all -- they're Go standard-library CVEs tied to the go1.25.1
toolchain itself (encoding/asn1, net/url, encoding/pem, crypto/tls,
crypto/x509, etc.), fixed across go1.25.2 through go1.25.12. Flagged then
as a bigger, separate change; doing it now.

Installed go1.25.12 in user-space (go install golang.org/dl/go1.25.12@latest
&& go1.25.12 download, no root needed) and rebuilt/retested both modules
with it BEFORE changing anything committed. Confirmed 0 regressions, then:
- go.mod `go` directive bumped to 1.25.12 in both modules (go mod edit -go=)
- go/Dockerfile's pinned base image digest updated to golang:1.25.12-trixie
  (fetched via the real Docker Hub registry API, not guessed)
- go/Dockerfile.siblings (same component, alt build path) given the same
  digest bump for consistency
- proxy/Dockerfile version-bumped (kept intentionally unpinned, per that
  file's own stated dev-convenience design -- not converted to a hard pin)
- .github/workflows/ci.yml's go-version bumped in both go/tools jobs

govulncheck ./... after: go/ dropped from 21 reachable vulnerabilities to
**0**. tools/ separately had one non-stdlib reachable finding left
(GO-2026-6061 in google.golang.org/grpc, reachable via cmd/start-proxy's
init.Init()) -- bumped v1.79.1 -> v1.82.1 via go get + go mod tidy. Both
modules are now fully clean of every reachable vulnerability govulncheck
can find; only unreachable ("modules you require, but your code doesn't
call") findings remain in either, same honest caveat govulncheck itself
gives for those.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Run gitleaks/semgrep/slither for real; fix what they found, document the rest

Closes another "not at all done" audit item -- the original audit couldn't
run these tools in its own environment. Installed gitleaks (already
present), semgrep and slither-analyzer (via a uv-managed venv, since this
environment's pip is externally-managed and apt needs sudo this session
doesn't have). ShellCheck/TruffleHog still couldn't be installed either --
tracked as a remaining gap, not silently dropped.

gitleaks: 9 raw findings (working tree) + 12 (git history), all reviewed --
zero real secrets. The one real private key found is gitignored and
unfunded; the rest are well-known public devnet/test-framework convention
keys (Hardhat's, forge-std's own).

semgrep: 18 findings, 615 rules, zero in contracts/. Fixed the two real,
in-scope ones: every GitHub Action in ci.yml pinned to a real commit SHA
(resolved via the GitHub API) instead of a mutable tag -- the exact
supply-chain pattern behind the tj-actions/changed-files and
reviewdog/action-setup incidents; pnpm-workspace.yaml hardened
(blockExoticSubdeps/minimumReleaseAge/trustPolicy), confirmed pnpm 9.15.9
(the currently-pinned version) tolerates these forward-compatible settings
rather than erroring before adding them. The rest were scaffold-owned code
this project doesn't use (python/, testing/) or a content-type false
positive on the scaffold's own DO-NOT-MODIFY boilerplate.

slither: 64 raw results against WorkProofEscrow.sol's full import closure,
almost all in vendored periphery-package interfaces. The one real,
in-contract finding worth real scrutiny -- reentrancy-eth on
dispatchVerification writing state after its external sendInstructions
call -- is already mitigated (nonReentrant) and already has a dedicated
passing adversarial test (testMaliciousExtensionRegistryCannotReenterDispatch),
not just asserted safe. Every other in-contract finding (uninitialized-local,
unused-return, calls-loop/costly-loop in the scaffold's own setExtensionId,
timestamp comparisons) reviewed and is a benign/idiomatic pattern or an
already-accepted, already-reviewed tradeoff, not a new bug.

Full disposition of every finding in docs/security/static-analysis.md.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Finish the two "partially done" audit items: canonical return validation + real invariant tests

Canonical return validation (the last unfixed piece of repair item 3, which
bundled revert/RPC distinction + value + per-call timeouts + this -- the
first three were already fixed): executeErc165 accepted any response with
result[31]==1 as supports=true regardless of what the other 31 bytes
contained or whether the response was even the right length -- a
garbage-padded or wrong-length response could be silently treated as a
canonically-encoded bool. Fixed with go-ethereum's own strict ABI bool
decoder (accounts/abi.readBool semantics), not a hand-rolled check. 5 new
tests, 3 confirmed load-bearing via meta-check.

Real Foundry invariant tests (closes "0 invariant functions", the other
partially-done item): test/WorkProofEscrowInvariant.t.sol adds a stateful
handler driving arbitrary interleaved sequences across many jobs at once
(create/accept/submit/lock/dispatch/settle-with-a-real-TEE-signed-verdict/
refund/cancel), reaching cross-job bugs the existing single-job
testFuzzSolvencyAndSinglePayout structurally cannot. Three invariants,
256 runs x 500 calls each: solvency (independent ghost-accounting ledger
vs. real escrow balance), no job ever both pays and refunds, and the
contract's own settled flag agrees with every outcome the handler actually
observed. Confirmed solvency is load-bearing by injecting a 1-unit
untracked leak into the real payout path and watching it fail with the
exact expected off-by-one, with Foundry's shrinker finding an 8-call
minimal repro -- a first meta-check attempt (doubling the payout) revealed
a real methodology bug before that: it just made the transfer revert on
insufficient balance, silently absorbed by the handler's own try/catch, so
it never actually exercised anything. Contract restored to byte-identical
(diffed against HEAD) after both attempts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Bump vulnerable filippo.io/edwards25519 and golang.org/x/crypto (audit finding)

Installed govulncheck for real (it wasn't available when the original audit
flagged these) and ran it before touching anything: neither edwards25519's
GO-2026-4503 nor x/crypto's several ssh/openpgp advisories were actually
reachable from WorkProof's own call paths in either module -- both only
showed up under "modules you require, but your code doesn't appear to
call". Bumped anyway (edwards25519 v1.1.0->v1.2.0 in both go/ and tools/;
x/crypto v0.50.0->v0.54.0 in go/, tools/ was already on v0.54.0) since
they're trivial, low-risk indirect-dependency version bumps.

Bumping x/crypto transitively pulled golang.org/x/text v0.36.0->v0.40.0 in
go/, which turned out to fix a genuinely *reachable* vulnerability
(GO-2026-5970, an infinite loop reachable via internal/extension's own
init-time call chain) that govulncheck surfaced along the way -- not
something the original audit had flagged, found only because the tool was
actually run this time.

Also surfacing, not yet fixed (out of scope for this specific ask): go/'s
remaining 21 reachable vulnerabilities are all Go standard-library CVEs
tied to the go1.25.1 toolchain itself, fixable only by a toolchain bump
(which also touches the pinned Docker base image digest) -- a materially
bigger change than a dependency version bump. tools/ separately has one
reachable non-stdlib finding in google.golang.org/grpc, unrelated to either
originally-flagged package.

Fix CI: Tools job also needs helloworld's bindings, not just workproofescrow's

tools/pkg/utils/instructions.go (original scaffold code, still compiled as
part of the tools/ module) imports the helloworld package -- its abigen
bindings are also gitignored/generated, and the tools job only ever
regenerated workproofescrow's. Confirmed via the actual failed CI run
(go vet: undefined: helloworld.NewHelloWorldInstructionSender and similar),
then reproduced and fixed locally against a genuinely clean state (moved
both binding sets aside this time, not just workproofescrow's -- the
previous local check had the same blind spot the real CI run just exposed).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix CI: forge build still failed even with submodules: recursive

lib/flare-foundry-periphery-package manages its own OpenZeppelin/LayerZero
dependencies via soldeer, not nested git submodules -- its dependencies/
directory is gitignored inside that submodule's own repo and only exists
after running forge soldeer install. submodules: recursive alone (the
previous fix) fetches the submodule's tracked files but not this --
confirmed by watching the actual CI run fail on missing OpenZeppelin
imports after that fix was already pushed, then reproducing the exact
failure locally (moved dependencies/ aside, forge build failed the same
way) before confirming forge soldeer install (run from inside the
submodule) fixes it.

Added `forge soldeer install` before every forge build in the contracts,
go, and tools jobs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix CI: submodule checkout was missing, coverage/tools/full-workspace never ran

forge build in the contracts job was failing on every push/PR since Phase 3
added lib/flare-foundry-periphery-package as a git submodule -- actions/
checkout@v4 doesn't fetch submodules by default, and nothing here ever
opted in. Confirmed by actually removing the checked-out submodule locally
and reproducing the failure before fixing it.

Also, per the same independent audit: CI never ran forge test (only build),
never ran coverage, never built/tested tools/ at all, and only tested
packages/schema instead of the full pnpm workspace. All fixed:

- contracts: submodules: recursive on checkout; added forge test and
  forge coverage --ir-minimum (RealRegistryFork.t.sol forks live Coston2
  read-only, no secrets needed).
- go: submodules: recursive; generates the abigen bindings (gitignored,
  not committed) via scripts/generate-workproof-bindings.sh before
  building -- confirmed this step is load-bearing by actually removing the
  generated files locally and reproducing the resulting compile failure
  first. Replaced `go fmt` (silently rewrites and never fails) with a real
  gofmt -l check, and added go vet and -race.
- tools (new job): same binding-generation + gofmt/vet/test pattern. The
  gofmt check surfaced 5 pre-existing scaffold files (never touched this
  project) that were already non-compliant -- fixed with gofmt -w rather
  than working around the check, since gofmt changes are whitespace-only.
- schemas: pnpm -r test instead of --dir packages/schema, so relayer/
  web/test-bundle-sdk are honestly exercised too (they report "0 tests"
  today, which is accurate, not hidden).

Every job's steps were run locally against a simulated clean checkout
(generated bindings moved aside, regenerated via the actual CI commands)
before this was pushed, not assumed to work from the YAML alone.

Complete Phase 3 production contracts + Phase 4 Go verifier, then fix four release-blocking defects found by independent audit

Phase 3: WorkProofEscrow.sol rewritten around real production dependencies
(FTestXRP/Relay/RandomNumberV2 resolved live via ContractRegistry, TEE
selected+pinned at createJob and never silently re-selected, real dispatch
through ITeeExtensionRegistry.sendInstructions, nonReentrant on every
fund-moving path, validated treasury instead of the Phase 2 lab's
unrecoverable hash-derived placeholder). 97 tests (80 local + 10 spike + 7
real Coston2 fork), all green.

Phase 4: go/internal/verifier — the WORKPROOF/VERIFY handler. Bundle schema
validation + real RFC 8785 (gowebpki/jcs) canonicalization, the real
/decrypt client, an HTTPS-only allowlisted ciphertext fetcher, independent
on-chain re-verification of random number/job state, deterministic
Fisher-Yates vector selection, and VerdictV1 production. Found and fixed a
real gap mid-phase: JobTerms/WorkProofInstruction were missing
ciphertextHash despite SPEC.md requiring it; fixing it also surfaced that
the Solidity optimizer had never been enabled, which had left bytecode on a
44-byte EIP-170 margin.

Independent audit (2026-08-09): every finding checked against source was
accurate. Four release-blocking defects fixed:
- verdictIdentityFrom never set InstructionId, so every Go-produced verdict
  had a zero instructionId -- WorkProofEscrow.sol's signature recovery
  (which reconstructs the digest using v.id.instructionId from the decoded
  data) always recovered the wrong signer. No Go-generated result could
  ever have settled. Fixed by threading the real ActionResult.ID through
  from processVerify.
- settleAttempt only checked the dispatch timeout, never graceEnds -- a
  late Pass could pay the contractor after the client's refund deadline
  had passed. Fixed with an explicit guard, exact-boundary tests, and a
  test proving the client wins the race via refundExpired instead.
- executeEthCallReverts treated any RPC/transport error identically to a
  genuine EVM revert -- an outage or adversarial provider could force a
  false Pass. Fixed by distinguishing real JSON-RPC reverts (rpc.Error)
  from transport failures via a fake-RPC-server test suite. msg.value was
  also validated by schema but silently never applied to calls -- fixed.
- The deployment pipeline (pre-build.sh, tools/cmd/deploy-contract) deployed
  the scaffold's sample HelloWorldInstructionSender, never WorkProofEscrow --
  confirmed firsthand by actually running it. Added a WorkProof-specific
  deploy path (tools/cmd/deploy-workproof-escrow,
  tools/cmd/set-workproof-extension-id); register-extension itself turned
  out to already be fully generic. Verified for real against live Coston2:
  resolves the real FlareTeeManager diamond and configured treasury/fee,
  fails honestly at the known funding blocker, never touches HelloWorld.

Plus five high-severity fixes: bundle.PublicSpecHash was never bound to the
job's real specHash; EngineVersionHash was echoed from client input instead
of the verifier's real running version; the ciphertext fetcher's
DNS-rebinding defense re-resolved DNS at connect time instead of pinning
the validated IP (a real TOCTOU gap despite the original doc comment's
claim to have closed it); MaxBundleBytes/TimeoutMsPerCall/the ERC-165
vector's gas cap were validated but never enforced; the release image's
base layer and the Solidity compiler version were both unpinned. Verifier
coverage rose from 32.5% to 43.6%, driven entirely by new tests for each
fix, several confirmed load-bearing via meta-check (temporarily revert the
fix, confirm the new test fails, restore it).

Both evidence docs now carry explicit "Post-audit corrections" sections
rather than silently editing away the original overclaims. Full detail in
NEW_WORK.md "Post-audit remediation". Not yet done: 0 Foundry invariant
functions (stated plainly, not hidden); the relayer/web UI/public
repo/judge-flow product surface (out of scope for this pass); funding and
Coston2 indexer credentials remain externally blocked
(docs/operations/external-dependencies.md).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Complete Phase 1 freeze + Phase 2 validation lab, incl. mandatory FCC signature spike

Phase 1: SPEC.md/THREAT_MODEL.md/NEW_WORK.md, VerdictV1/bundle/demo-evidence
schemas with generated Go/TS/Solidity fixtures, CI, dependency/secret-scan
docs, repo layout for schema/relayer/web/deployments/evidence/operations.

Phase 2: the plan's mandatory FCC ActionResult signature-compatibility spike
is proven green — contracts/lib/FccVerdict.sol reconstructs the real signing
chain (packed digest -> EIP-191 wrap -> canonical/low-S recovery) from pinned
tee-node v0.0.24 / go-flare-common source, verified against both a real
Go-signed vector (go/cmd/fcc-spike, test/FccSignatureSpike.t.sol) and dynamic
vm.sign-based verdicts (test/WorkProofEscrow.t.sol). WorkProofEscrow.sol's
settle() now binds the full VerdictV1 schema instead of a placeholder digest.
All 10 Phase 2 required simulations plus a fuzzed accounting invariant pass
(29/29 tests). Added a pause mechanism that never blocks refund/cancel/
already-dispatched settlement.

Two real bugs caught and fixed during this work: a truncated
SECP256K1_HALF_N constant that rejected nearly all valid signatures, and a
test-harness chain-ID mismatch that made mutation tests pass for the wrong
reason (caught via a meta-check that temporarily disabled a real check and
confirmed its test failed).

Remaining before Phase 2 can be called fully closed: no handler-based
forge-invariant suite (WorkProofInvariantTest per the plan's exit-condition
commands), no SIMULATION_ONLY UI banner (no UI yet). Both documented in
docs/evidence/phase2-simulation.md, not hidden.
